subject: SIG audit: compact IR evidence bundle & redacted telemetry request
messages:
From: Natalie Brooks <natalie.brooks@finvault.com>
To: evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Cc: audit_team@finvault.com
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 08:02:00 -0400
Subject: SIG audit: compact IR evidence bundle & redacted telemetry request

Hi Evelyn,

We have a SIG audit kickoff next week and the audit team has one targeted ask before the tabletop: a compact incident response (IR) runbook excerpt and a small, redacted telemetry snapshot for an M-1 incident we discussed in the pre-kickoff call. Specifically they want:

- A short IR runbook excerpt (1–2 pages) showing escalation steps, SLO owners, and retention class for forensic artifacts.
- A redacted telemetry snapshot limited to 1 hour around the incident window (timestamps only, no PII or full traces) and a CSV sample of access logs (200 rows max) that demonstrates how we map internal IDs to customer tenants.

Can Redwood provide a zip with these artifacts by Monday EOD PST? The SIG reviewers will only accept compact, redacted sets — anything that looks like a full forensic dump will be kicked back.

We appreciate the quick turnaround. If there are gating approvals or a dedicated contact for CISO-level questions, please let us know.

Thanks,
Natalie Brooks
Senior Audit Manager, FinVault
---
FinVault | audit_team@finvault.com
From: evelyn.hart@redwood.com <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG audit: compact IR evidence bundle & redacted telemetry request

Hi Natalie —

Thanks for the heads up and the clear constraints. We'll put together a slim bundle that meets the SIG requirements and does not include any raw PII or complete trace payloads. Plan below: 

1) IR runbook excerpt (PDF): single-page escalation matrix + ownership + retention class.
2) Telemetry snapshot (JSONL, redacted): timestamps, event types, coarse metric buckets; no request/response bodies or tokens.
3) Access logs sample (CSV): 200 rows with hashed internal IDs; we'll include mapping notes describing hashing algorithm and where full mappings are retained (enterprise only, not included in the bundle).

I'll own the package delivery. Marissa, can you produce the redacted telemetry slice and sample logs? Karthik, please review the IR excerpt and sign off on retention language.

We should also include a short chain-of-custody note and an itemized index to make the reviewer's job faster.

EOD Monday PST is tight but doable. If you need earlier, tell us the absolute cutoff and we'll prioritize.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG audit: compact IR evidence bundle & redacted telemetry request

Eve —

I pulled a 90-minute slice around the M-1 window (2026-07-17 14:30–16:00 UTC) and ran the redaction pipeline. Deliverables in draft:

- sanitized-telemetry-20260717.jsonl (timestamps, event_type, metric_bucket, hashed_user_id) — ~22k lines but we will trim to the 1-hour window requested and provide a sampler that represents the event distribution.
- access_logs_sample.csv — 200 rows (hashes for internal_id, tenant_id replaced by tenant aliases).

Notes: we used SHA-256 + salt for hashing; full mapping is available to the security team in a secure vault (separate request required). No network packet captures or request payloads are included.

I will attach the sampler and the CSV in the package and include a short README describing redaction steps. Evelyn — I put a draft README and chain_of_custody.txt in a shared Drive link; do you want me to inline those in the zip or just reference the Drive link?

Marissa
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Natalie —

Attached is the compact evidence bundle for the SIG reviewers. What you'll find in the zip (IR_compact_bundle_20260720.zip):

- IRP_excerpt_v1.pdf (1 page): escalation matrix, SLO owners, retention classes.
- sanitized-telemetry-20260717.jsonl (1-hour sampler) — 3600 lines representing event timestamps + event_type + metric_bucket + hashed_id.
- access_logs_sample.csv (200 rows) — hashed internal ids and tenant aliases only.
- chain_of_custody.txt (plain text) — who extracted, redaction steps, and storage path for full mappings.
- README_redaction.txt — short explanation of algorithms and how to request elevated access.

A few implementation notes for your reviewers:
- We did not include request/response bodies or parameter values.
- Hashing: SHA-256 with per-run salt; full mapping only available to security and will not be shared to auditors without an executed NDA + written approval.
- Retention: forensic artifacts are retained 90 days by default; longer retention is available under Enterprise contracts and noted in the IR excerpt.

Karthik performed a quick policy review for the IR excerpt and suggested one minor wording tweak around SLA exceptions (already applied).

If the SIG team needs an expanded slice (e.g., 4 hours) or a short Q&A call to validate redaction, we can make time tomorrow morning PST.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: IR_compact_bundle_20260720.zip (contains IRP_excerpt_v1.pdf, sanitized-telemetry-20260717.jsonl, access_logs_sample.csv, chain_of_custody.txt, README_redaction.txt)
